note: P4213 (Pro 23:8) — you will vomit up the morsels, and waste your pleasant words.

dims.v: wasted graciousness — the kind words spent in vain on a grudging host
the pleasant/gracious words the guest spends on the miser — wasted, once the false welcome is seen for what it is, along with the very morsels eaten
(the grudging host on whom they are wasted)
the graciousness squandered on one whose heart was never in it

naem (pleasant/sweet) — 'and waste your PLEASANT words'; the courtesy and gracious speech spent on a grudging host is thrown away, and the meal itself becomes nausea. Graciousness is wasted where the heart is closed.
